lede: Montréal had last change, so Martin St. Louis picked most of these matchups. Montréal played without Kirby Dach and Mike Matheson. Pittsburgh played without Elmer Söderblom and Ilya Solovyov.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Robertson’s line
notes.text: Martin St. Louis sent F. Xhekaj, Kapanen and Beck out for 4:10 of their 7:40 at 5-on-5 against Dewar, Lizotte and Robertson (54%, about 18% with no line matching). Montréal scored one of its five goals then.

notes.head: Bolduc’s line drew Malkin’s line
notes.text: Bolduc, Danault and Texier spent 6:32 of their 11:26 at 5-on-5 against Chinakhov, Kindel and Malkin (57%, about 26% with no line matching).

notes.head: Caufield’s line drew Crosby’s line
notes.text: Caufield, Newhook and Slafkovský spent 7:45 of their 12:08 at 5-on-5 against Novak, Crosby and Rakell (64%, about 33% with no line matching), and they had the worse of the chances, 0.31 to 0.97 expected goals. Pittsburgh scored two of its four goals then.

notes.head: One matchup paid off
notes.text: Kreider, Evans and Anderson kept drawing Pittsburgh’s third line, Kuzmenko, Lapierre and Koivunen. In those 5:49 Montréal had 0.72 expected goals to Pittsburgh’s 0.05. Montréal scored two of its five goals then.

foot: Martin St. Louis matched about as hard as in his other home games: each line spent 56% of its time against one opposing line, against 40% to 61% in his first six.
